task.goal: Increase delimiter-counting throughput without changing quoted-field behavior.
task.context: A JavaScript CSV scanner counts delimiters outside quoted fields. The baseline is correct but allocates an array for every input.

constraints.text: Quoted delimiters and escaped quotes must retain baseline behavior.

success.text: Repeated throughput is higher than the allocation-heavy baseline.
The correctness probe passes all quoted-field cases.

candidates.title: Count delimiters with one regex
candidates.summary: Replace the allocating state scan with a compact native regex.
candidates.mechanism: Use a global comma regex and return the number of matches.
assumptions: Native regex scanning dominates a JavaScript loop
risks: The shortcut may count delimiters inside quoted fields
validation: Run quoted-field and escaped-quote correctness cases.
Measure repeated throughput against the baseline.

candidates.title: Use an allocation-free indexed state machine
candidates.summary: Preserve quote state while scanning code units without an intermediate array.
candidates.mechanism: Walk the input by index, track quoted state, and skip escaped quote pairs.
assumptions: Array materialization is a material baseline cost
risks: Quote transition logic could diverge from the baseline
validation: Run quoted-field and escaped-quote correctness cases.
Measure repeated throughput against the baseline.

decisions.title: Use an allocation-free indexed state machine
